after:
(i) *Spatial, bounded case.* Put $r_s:=2s+1$, $S_N:=(\mathbb C^{r_s})^{\otimes N}$ and $M:=r_s^N$. The finite product spin basis identifies $S_N$ with $\mathbb C^M$. Use the full finite-component product unitary
$$\Theta_N:H^{\otimes N}\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M),\qquad [\Theta_N(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_N)]_a(X)=\prod_{j=1}^N[f_j(x_j)]_{a_j},$$
where $a\in\{1,\dots,r_s\}^N$. Its construction and combined spatial/spin permutation action are proved in [[lem-nrqm-many-body-finite-spin-product-identification]], from the finite-component extension of [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]. Let $H_{\mathrm{sc}}:=K+M_V$ be the scalar operator of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]] (a), (b) for the potential $V(X)=\sum_iV_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_i)+\sum_{i<j}W(x_i-x_j)$, and define the labelled operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=H_{\mathrm{sc}}\otimes I_{S_N}$ in the finite component reading. Clause (c) of that supplier, with component count $M$, gives self-adjointness on
$$D(H_{\mathrm{lab}})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)=D(K)\otimes S_N,$$
and the lower bound $-\|V\|_\infty$. Equal masses, identical external potentials and the even pair potential make the scalar domain and operator invariant under spatial block permutations. The finite-component lemma shows that the combined permutations $\mathcal U_\pi=\Theta_NU_\pi\Theta_N^{-1}$ also permute the spin slots and commute with $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ on its domain. Thus $\mathcal P_\sigma:=\Theta_NP_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta_N^{-1}$ reduces the operator by [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]] (a)-(d), and the transported sector energy is
$$H_N^{\sigma,\mathrm{coord}}:=H_{\mathrm{lab}}\big|_{D(H_{\mathrm{lab}})\cap\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\sigma}.$$
It is self-adjoint on $\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\sigma=\Theta_N\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, with the zero operator on the zero-sector branch. The model's tensor reading is $H_N^\sigma:=\Theta_N^{-1}H_N^{\sigma,\mathrm{coord}}\Theta_N$ on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$. Every constant spin action commutes with the spin-independent labelled operator; a common spin unitary $A^{\otimes N}$ preserves each identical-particle sector by the finite-component lemma. For $s=0$, $M=1$ and this is the scalar product reading; for $N=1$, $M=2s+1$ and it is the one-particle component reading.

(ii) *Spatial Coulomb case.* Keep the same $S_N$, $M$, $\Theta_N$ and combined permutations. For the singular data of clause (c)(ii), take the scalar $H_{\mathrm{sc}}:=K+M_V$ of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]] (b), and let $H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=H_{\mathrm{sc}}\otimes I_{S_N}$. Clause (c) of that supplier, with component count $M$, gives self-adjointness and a lower bound on $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$. Its permutation invariance for equal masses and species-invariant coefficients in (d), together with the constant spin permutation of the finite-component lemma, gives reduction by $\mathcal P_\sigma$. Define the coordinate sector restriction and its tensor transport exactly as in (i); the domain is the intersection with the same component Sobolev space, and both the nonzero- and zero-sector branches are retained. No spin dependence is introduced into the singular interaction.
